resources.name: Anki
resources.description: Flashcard app with spaced repetition for code words and phrases.
resources.descriptionLong: Create cards for letter and code word pairs, Q codes, or radio phrases. Anki schedules reviews based on how well you answer.

resources.name: Quizlet
resources.description: Public card sets and short quizzes for the NATO alphabet.
resources.descriptionLong: Search for sets on code words, Q codes, and Morse, or build your own set and study it on the web or in the app.

resources.name: AnkiWeb Shared Decks
resources.description: Browse community decks for code words and radio phrases.
resources.descriptionLong: AnkiWeb hosts decks uploaded by learners. Search by topic, read the card list, and download a deck into Anki.
resources.notes: Check the card contents before studying a shared deck.

resources.name: NATO Phonetic Alphabet table
resources.description: Letter, code word, and pronunciation table.
resources.descriptionLong: The Wikipedia article lists the full alphabet with pronunciation notes and background on its use in voice communication.
resources.notes: Use the table as the source for your own cards.

resources.name: Q code reference
resources.description: Lookup table for three letter radio abbreviations.
resources.descriptionLong: The article explains the origins of Q codes and lists the abbreviations still used in radio and aviation.

resources.name: Morse code reference
resources.description: Letters, numbers, and punctuation in Morse code.
resources.descriptionLong: Wikipedia gives the International Morse code alphabet, its timing rules, and a short history of the code.

resources.name: Prosigns reference
resources.description: Morse prosigns and what they mean.
resources.descriptionLong: Prosigns are Morse sequences sent as one signal. The article lists the common prosigns used by Morse operators.

resources.name: ARRL Getting Licensed
resources.description: Amateur radio licence study information from ARRL.
resources.descriptionLong: ARRL explains US licence classes, exams, and study material on its getting licensed page.

resources.name: FAA Publications
resources.description: Official FAA manuals, handbooks, and reference material.
resources.descriptionLong: The FAA publications library hosts air traffic and pilot documents that define standard radio phraseology.

resources.name: ITU Radiocommunication Sector
resources.description: International radio rules and spectrum information.
resources.descriptionLong: The ITU-R site covers radiocommunication standards and the study groups that sit behind international radio practice.

resources.name: Aviation English
resources.description: Background on English language requirements in aviation.
resources.descriptionLong: The article explains why standard English phraseology is used for international flights and how it is assessed.

resources.name: Ham Radio Crash Course
resources.description: YouTube channel on amateur radio equipment and operating.
resources.descriptionLong: Video lessons cover ham radio basics, gear, and on air practice. Use them alongside your own code word drills.

resources.name: Phonetic alphabets
resources.description: Overview of spelling alphabets and how they differ.
resources.descriptionLong: The article places the NATO alphabet alongside other alphabets used for clear voice communication.

resources.name: Anki
resources.description: Desktop and mobile flashcard apps for daily drills.
resources.descriptionLong: Use Anki on a computer or phone to type your own answers and keep a review history for code words and phrases.

resources.name: Quizlet web app
resources.description: Browser based card sets with write mode practice.
resources.descriptionLong: Quizlet write mode asks you to type answers from a set, which suits callsign spelling practice.

resources.name: AOPA
resources.description: Pilot association with training and safety articles.
resources.descriptionLong: AOPA publishes articles on pilot training, aircraft operations, and safety.
resources.notes: Browsing the site is open, while some member services need a subscription.

resources.name: FAA Handbooks and Manuals
resources.description: Free pilot handbooks and training manuals.
resources.descriptionLong: The FAA library has downloadable handbooks that cover communications and standard procedures.

resources.name: International Telecommunication Union
resources.description: Global body coordinating radio spectrum and telecom rules.
resources.descriptionLong: The ITU site provides background on international radiocommunication and the rules that govern spectrum use.

resources.name: Radiotelephony procedure
resources.description: Overview of standard voice procedures.
resources.descriptionLong: The article describes call signs, readbacks, and procedural words used in two way radio communication.

resources.name: Call sign reference
resources.description: How call signs are assigned and structured.
resources.descriptionLong: Wikipedia explains amateur, aviation, and marine call sign formats with examples.

resources.name: Morse code practice videos
resources.description: Video search results for Morse practice audio.
resources.descriptionLong: Use the search page to find slow Morse lessons, code practice sessions, and keying demonstrations.
